claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you are claiming Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to level 3) or on an approved training course? Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in qualifying education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in school anymore - they're not doing A-levels or anything like that. They've actually started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 17 and has started an apprenticeship, I need to ask one more important question.

Is Alex's apprenticeship an **unpaid** approved training course (such as certain government-funded training schemes), or is it a **paid apprenticeship** where they receive a wage?

This distinction is important because Child Benefit can only continue for children on certain approved, unpaid training programmes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a paid apprenticeship - they get a wage for it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Let me just check the official guidance to make sure I give you accurate information about Alex's situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official guidance, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

The rules are clear that Child Benefit **stops** when a child:
- Starts an apprenticeship in England, or
- Starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training

Since Alex is 17, no longer in approved education, and has started a **paid apprenticeship**, you would unfortunately not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of the UK Child Benefit rules, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:** Alex is 17 years old, has left approved education, and has started a paid apprenticeship. Under the Child Benefit rules, eligibility ends when a child starts an apprenticeship in England, or when they start paid work (24+ hours per week) while no longer in approved education or training.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if they return to full-time approved education before age 20—you may be able to claim again at that point.

I'm sorry this isn't better news. If you have any other questions or if there's anything else I can help you with, please let me know.
